# Packages tested together share one test binary, even when one package's
# tests import another. What a package's _test.go files initialize belongs
# to that package's run: it runs in that package's directory, after the
# package itself, and never in another package's run.

go test -x ./reader ./other ./lib
stdout '^ok\s+example.com/grouped/reader'
stdout '^ok\s+example.com/grouped/other'
stdout '^ok\s+example.com/grouped/lib'
stderr -count=1 'link -o'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/grouped

go 1.27
-- reader/testdata/data.txt --
reader's own data
-- reader/reader.go --
package reader

var Ready string

func init() { Ready = "reader" }
-- reader/reader_test.go --
package reader

import (
	"os"
	"testing"
)

// data reads a file relative to this package's directory as the package
// initializes: every other package's run would fail on it.
var data = mustRead("testdata/data.txt")

func mustRead(name string) string {
	body, err := os.ReadFile(name)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	return string(body)
}

// seen is what the package's own initialization had done when the test file's
// initialization ran.
var seen = Ready

func TestData(test *testing.T) {
	if data != "reader's own data\n" {
		test.Fatalf("data = %q", data)
	}
	if seen != "reader" {
		test.Fatalf("the test file initialized before the package: seen %q", seen)
	}
}
-- other/other_test.go --
package other

import (
	"testing"

	"example.com/grouped/lib"
	"example.com/grouped/reader"
)

func TestOther(test *testing.T) {
	if reader.Ready != "reader" {
		test.Fatalf("reader.Ready = %q", reader.Ready)
	}
	if lib.TestFileRan {
		test.Fatal("lib's test file initialized in other's run")
	}
}
-- lib/lib.go --
package lib

// TestFileRan is set by lib's own test file as it initializes.
var TestFileRan bool
-- lib/lib_test.go --
package lib

import "testing"

func init() { TestFileRan = true }

func TestLib(test *testing.T) {
	if !TestFileRan {
		test.Fatal("lib's test file did not initialize in lib's run")
	}
}
